title: Progressive Risk Estimation for Accident Anticipation
claim: Baseline scores stay high and noisy even in safe driving, while ours rises gradually as the event nears.
layout: 2 stacked parts: score-vs-time plot above, two aligned frame rows below
description: The top panel is a line plot of Score (0 to 1) against Time in seconds. A red baseline curve stays noisy and high, between about 0.4 and 0.9, throughout the normal-driving period. A teal curve for the proposed method stays low, around 0.1 to 0.3, then climbs gradually toward 1 as the crash approaches. A green vertical line marks t_ai, the anomaly start. A red vertical line marks t_acc, the accident time. Five black dots on the time axis connect through dashed gray arrows to dashboard-camera frames below. The frames form two aligned rows. The Baseline row is labeled in red and has blue borders. The PRE-ACT row is labeled in teal and has red borders. The PRE-ACT frames are tinted blue when the score is low and red when it is high, while the baseline frames show little change. The eye goes first to the two contrasting curves.
caption: \ours: From binary accident prediction to progressive risk anticipation. Unlike the dominant paradigm of formulating accident anticipation as a binary classification of whether an accident will occur (baseline), we model risk as a temporally evolving signal that reflects when an accident is likely to occur. By explicitly enforcing temporal order and distance-to-crash awareness, our model reduces false alarms while progressively increasing risk as abnormal cues emerge. Scores are overlaid on frames as an alpha channel, with blue indicating safe and red indicating risky predictions.
abstract: Accident anticipation aims to recognize anomalous driving cues before a crash while avoiding false alarms during normal driving. Existing approaches typically formulate this task as binary classification, focusing on whether an accident will occur rather than when it will occur. We propose PRE-ACT, a framework that models accident risk as a continuously evolving signal that increases as the crash approaches. By explicitly enforcing temporal ordering and distance-to-accident awareness, our method progressively raises risk while suppressing premature alarms, leading to significant improvements on MM-AU subsets and Nexar. We further introduce a Separation Score to evaluate the global behavior of predicted risk curves beyond local temporal windows. Code and visualizations are available at https://github.com/giddyyupp/PRE-ACT.
